input_references.role: Timestamped GPS points with map-matched road coordinates and OSM way identifiers

metadata.goal: Analyze patterns of exploration and return visits across the supplied user histories.
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed WorldTrace case with 250 trajectories. Route geometries come from observed NYC WorldTrace records and retain map-matched coordinates and OSM way identifiers. User, visit sequence, time, mode, vehicle, and weather context are arranged to realize the stated analysis goal.

insight_list.insight: Most observed visits return to previously visited areas, while only a smaller share expands the user's visited-location set.

plot.title: Newly Visited Location Patterns: Insight 1
plot.description: The geographic panel uses map-matched WorldTrace route geometry; the question-specific statistical plot summarizes the corresponding pattern.

insight_list.question: Across the five users, what share of trajectories revisit familiar locations rather than expand the visited-location set?
insight_list.actionable_insight: Compare new-location and return-visit counts for the complete histories.
insight_list.code: counts=df['is_new_location_visit'].value_counts().rename(index={False:'return visit',True:'new-location visit'}); print(counts); print('new share',df.is_new_location_visit.mean()); counts.plot.bar(color=['#2563eb','#f97316']); plt.ylabel('trajectories'); plt.show()

insight_list.insight: Exploration becomes progressively less frequent as the number of previously visited locations increases.
